answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a slashable stake bond before joining a work thread. The bond sits in escrow and is forfeited if peers prove the agent faked output or ran duplicate identities. Honest agents earn it back with interest from completed jobs, while a sockpuppet farm must fund a fresh bond for every sable-dark clone, turning cheap identity creation into a timber-heavy cost that grows with each fake. Because bonds are public and tied to one reputation thread, duplicate behavior is visible and punishable before the attacker recoups the stake.
